KaiHatch is an Android archive extractor built around genuine in-place extraction.
Unlike conventional extractors that keep the original archive intact while creating extracted files, Hatch Mode progressively reuses space from the archive itself.
This means you can extract supported archives with significantly less additional free storage.
You can also use Standard Mode for conventional extraction.
Important: Hatch Mode modifies the original archive. Interrupting extraction may leave it unrecoverable.

KaiHatch was inspired by the concept of progressive in-place archive extraction demonstrated by HatchZip (https://github.com/Fabiannez/HatchZip). KaiHatch is an independent Android implementation written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. It contains no HatchZip source code and has no official affiliation with or endorsement from the HatchZip project.
